title: Task routing table: categories to models, /routing modal with one searchable model list, keryx routing CLI; review and subagents read it

AC1.note: src/harness/routing/table.ts defines ROUTING_CATEGORIES (8 categories), CategoryAssignment union (session-default/model/provider-default), and resolveCategory/resolveCategoryDetailed applying override>project>user>default precedence, pure with no fs/network access. Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331; bun test src/harness/routing/table.test.ts (run as part of a 4-file, 74-pass batch) green.

AC2.note: src/harness/routing/config.ts's loadRoutingConfig/saveRoutingConfig share the project routing.config.json and per-user shell-config.ts entry through one loader; a malformed/unreadable file is a named, surfaced error (never a silent empty table), verified by config.test.ts's malformed-file tests. Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331.

AC3.note: src/commands/routing.ts implements keryx routing list [--json]/set/unset/trust mirroring providers.ts's subcommand dispatch shape, --user/--project selecting the write layer (default --user); list prints every category, resolution and source layer. Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331; bun test src/commands/routing.test.ts green (part of the 74-pass batch); exercised keryx routing --help/list myself this session.

AC4.note: /routing (ROUTING_COMMAND, src/tui/routing-inspector.ts) opens a modal-host list+detail modal; the list side shows every category and resolution, Enter opens a flat searchable picker built on mountFilterList (extracted to src/tui/filter-list.ts) fed every connected provider's models plus one provider-default row per provider and one session-default row; a confirmed pick writes immediately to the per-user layer. Proven by a real keyboard-driven modal test (routing-inspector.test.ts, otuiTest AC4) over a fixture multi-provider catalogue. Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331; bun test src/tui/routing-inspector.test.ts -> 11 pass, 0 fail.

AC5.note: runTier (src/commands/review.ts) resolves the review category via applyReviewRoutingCategory ahead of assignTier's own ranking; an explicit {kind:model} entry replaces the decision, session-default leaves it byte-identical (review.test.ts AC5 'with an EMPTY routing table' regression test), tagged routed:true (never tier_resolution: discovered) to avoid mislabeling. Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331; bun test src/commands/review.test.ts -t 'flow 305' -> 14 pass, 0 fail.

AC6.note: createSpawnSubagentTool (src/harness/tool/builtin/spawn-subagent-tool.ts) resolves the subagents category when the dispatcher supplied no model_tier (kind absent/inherit), constructing an explicit or tier ChildModelRequest via categoryAssignmentToChildModelRequest before calling resolveChildModel. Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331; bun test src/harness/tool/builtin/spawn-subagent-tool.test.ts -> 22 pass, 0 fail (AC6 test: subagents resolves to an allowed provider/model and the child actually runs on it).

AC7.note: The category-resolved ChildModelRequest passes through resolveChildModel's G1/G2/G3 gates unmodified; traced end to end (spawn-subagent-tool.ts -> orchestrate.ts spawnSubagent -> spawn.ts -> model.ts resolveChildModel). Original G1-out-of-allowlist scenario became unreachable once AC10 (same detected-provider source as G1's allowlist) pre-filters it; replaced with an equivalent G3 (classifiable, checked against the static provider registry, independent of AC10) denial test proving the gate chain still runs unmodified, plus a dispatcher-tier-overrides-category test. model.test.ts is byte-for-byte unchanged from pre-flow-305 main (45df98bd) and green (31 pass). Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331.

AC8.note: keryx routing is in COMMAND_DESCRIPTORS (src/standard/command-registry.ts) and HELP_GROUPS (src/standard/help-groups.ts, under Connect a model provider), /routing is in AGENT_SLASH_COMMANDS and the help modal; docs/docs/cli-reference.md and README.md describe the routing table, its two config layers, and explicit>project>user>default precedence, in English. command-registry.routing-categories.test.ts keeps the CLI's category enum in sync with ROUTING_CATEGORIES. Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331.

AC9.note: CI green (19 checks, per operator report on the squash-merged PR #705). keryx health run (run myself this session at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331): Code Health PASS, project score 94, no gate conditions triggered. spawn-subagent-tool.test.ts diff from pre-flow-305 main is additive-only (one import-line change, no existing assertion touched); review.test.ts diff is a pure addition block; model.test.ts is byte-for-byte unchanged. Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331.

AC10.note: resolveCategoryDetailed (src/harness/routing/table.ts) takes an optional ConnectedPredicate; every layer's assignment is checked in precedence order and an assignment naming an unconnected provider/model is treated as unresolved and falls through, all the way to session-default if needed. Wired at all four call sites (review tier, spawn_subagent, keryx routing list, /routing) via connectedPredicateFrom, each fed the same already-fetched provider-detection result (no new network probe); CLI/modal print '<provider>/<model> - not connected, falling back to <resolved>' via describeFallbackNotice. Tests cover each call site (table.test.ts, review.test.ts, spawn-subagent-tool.test.ts, routing.test.ts, routing-inspector.test.ts). Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331; full routing test batch (74+22+11+14 = 121 tests) green.

AC11.note: src/harness/routing/trust.ts (modelled on mcp-servers/trust.ts) fingerprints the validated project table (sha256, category- and key-sorted) and records per-user, per-project-root approvals in the operator's real global config dir (never under the project). loadRoutingConfig (config.ts) ignores an unapproved/changed project layer with a visible ROUTING_TRUST_NOTICE, surfaced in keryx routing list, /routing, and review tier output. keryx routing trust and /routing's t-then-y flow (armApproval/confirmApproval, routing-inspector.ts) both show every category via describeTableForApproval BEFORE recording approval. A routed review model is labelled routed: true, never tier_resolution: discovered. Round-2 review found and the operator fixed a real bypass (loadRoutingConfig skipped the trust check whenever the project file had any validation error, letting a valid-but-unapproved entry beside a malformed one take effect unapproved) in commit 97211c0ac30ffffdb593b454b5844fe3393942f8; verified fixed by reading that commit's diff and by running bun test src/harness/routing/config.test.ts -t 'a stray bad line never switches the gate off' (1 pass) and -t 'is refused, not carried along' (1 pass, the companion fix rejecting fields a kind does not define). Confirmed present at merge commit 31bab00fc167bc19ea212cd3eaf7e208ec0ca331.

AC10: "(new)" -> "An assignment at any layer that names a provider the operator has not connected (or a model that provider does not offer) is treated as unresolved at that layer and falls through to the next one, at every call site - `review tier`, `spawn_subagent`, `keryx routing list` and `/routing` - and the CLI and the modal show "<provider>/<model> - not connected, falling back to <resolved>"; tests cover each call site." (review of PR #705 (finding 1): the operator's fallback requirement from PRD section 5 was documented but not implemented and had not been carried into an AC)

AC11: "(new)" -> "A project `routing.config.json` takes effect only after the operator approves its current content once (a content hash recorded per user, like other project trust in keryx); until then, and whenever the file changes, its entries are ignored with a visible notice in `keryx routing list`, `/routing` and the review tier output, and `keryx routing trust` (or a confirmation in `/routing`) approves it; a routed review model is labelled as routed, never as discovered." (review of PR #705 (finding 2): a checked-in routing file could silently redirect the model that reviews the same diff)
